title: Symmetric Matrices and Quadratic Forms: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Symmetric Matrices and Quadratic Forms: Visual Guide

1. Eigenvectors Turn Perpendicular | the lower-left entry k of A = [1 1 ; k 2] dragged from -1 to 3, with both eigenvectors drawn from the origin and the readout showing the eigenvalues, the dot product, the angle between them, and the complex and defective regimes as they appear | symmetry is exactly what buys real eigenvalues and a right angle: the dot product is 1 - k and hits zero only at k = 1, the single value where A equals its own transpose, and the two-line proof that computes v2 transpose A v1 both ways is spelled out

2. Polynomial To Matrix | the three coefficients of q = a x^2 + b xy + c y^2 on sliders and a test vector chosen from four, with three matrices - the symmetric one, an upper-triangular rival, and their skew difference - each evaluated independently at that vector | the coefficient of a cross term is split across both off-diagonal slots, so building A from a polynomial means halving every cross coefficient; the lopsided rival returns the identical value at every x, which is why only the symmetric representative is unique and why x transpose B x equals x transpose (B + B transpose)/2 x

3. Signs Make Shape | the two eigenvalues and a rotation of the eigenvectors on sliders, with every point of the square coloured by the sign of q and the matrix, trace and determinant read out live | the eigenvalue signs alone decide the shape - all positive is a bowl, all negative a dome, mixed a saddle, a zero a flat trough - because in the eigenbasis q collapses to a weighted sum of squares; rotating the coordinates moves every entry of A but never the verdict, since P transpose A P is similar to A

4. Four Tests One Verdict | leading principal minors, trace and determinant, the eigenvalues themselves, and the completed square all computed at once from a, k and c, with seven presets including the k boundary and the all-entries-positive trap | the four tests always agree, so reach for the cheap one: Sylvester needs every leading principal minor positive (alternating from negative for negative definite), and a positive diagonal, a positive determinant or all-positive entries prove nothing on their own

5. Rebuild From Eigenvalues | two eigenvalues assigned to the fixed orthonormal pair q1 = (1,1)/sqrt2 and q2 = (1,-1)/sqrt2, with A, A squared, A + 3I and A inverse rebuilt as Q L Q transpose, plus x = c1 q1 + c2 q2 evaluated in the eigenbasis and again from the matrix entries | A = Q L Q transpose makes A a weighted sum of rank-one projections, so any function of A applies to the diagonal and leaves the eigenvectors untouched - squares, shifts and inverses all come free, and x transpose A x is just the eigenvalues weighted by the squared coordinates
